node.description: A node. The fields every node shares are described here, and one field a type names: the answer_options of a choice_question, typed by the conditional below. Every other field a type names is the type's own and is carried through untouched.

condition.description: An expression over context.* and responses.*. Whether it parses is a runtime finding.

key.description: How everything else names the node. A runtime holds it to [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and to being unique across the whole document; both are findings against an admitted document rather than reasons this is not a document.

nodes.description: The candidates of a container, considered in order.

type.description: An open string. This schema deliberately does not enumerate the node types: a host carrying a document through a validator older than one of its types should not have it rejected on the way. The runtime's registry is the other half of the rule - it does enumerate the types, and a type it does not know is a finding naming the type and the node, never a node quietly passed through.

answer_options.description: The options of a choice question, in the order the visitor is shown them. Each is an object whose value and label are strings where present; that the list is not empty, that each option carries both, that a value is in the key shape and unique among the question's options are findings against an admitted document. The conditional names the type in a required clause too, so a node naming no type is not held to it.

screen.description: A screen: its key, its title, and its nodes in order.

description: The structural contract of a screen document: the envelope, the screen, the common node fields, and the one field a type names that it types, the answer_options of a choice_question. It describes exactly what makes a JSON value a screen document at all, and nothing more. Everything a document can be wrong about - a key that is not lower snake case, a field a node's type requires, a heading level outside 1 to 6, a condition that does not parse, a template outside the subset, a type no runtime knows - is a finding a runtime raises against an admitted document, not a reason the value is not a document. A validator holding this schema and a runtime admitting the same value therefore agree: schema-valid means admitted.

kind.description: The content kind the document belongs to. An open string, and absent means screens: this schema deliberately does not enumerate the kinds, for the same reason it does not enumerate the node types - a host carrying a document through a validator older than one of its kinds should not have it rejected on the way. The runtime keeps the other half of the rule: it does enumerate the kinds it has a runtime for, and a kind it does not know is a finding against an admitted document naming the value, never a document resolved by the wrong kind's rules.

metadata.description: An open map. It carries name, description and domain as strings and a host may put what it likes beside them; a runtime neither interprets nor refuses the extras.

schema_version.description: The version of this contract the document was authored against. 1 in this version.

screens.description: The screens of the document, in the order a visitor is shown them.

title: Screen document
